subject: Request: Regional variant mandate and fallback carve-out for CareAtlas pilot
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CareAtlas ask — enforce regional variant + no-fallback for initial pilot

Evelyn / Grace —

Quick summary: CareAtlas wants us to lock their pilot traffic to a single US variant of the model (quantized v2-us-compact) and to disable automatic fallback to the hosted generic variant for the duration of the 6-week pilot. They say this is to ensure deterministic evaluation against their QA prompts and to avoid cross-variant behavior during clinical validation.

They've asked for this to be a hard routing decision (no automatic fallback) and explicit regional enforcement. Samira (CareAtlas) will sign an MOU if we can guarantee the variant binding and a rollback plan.

Can Product / SecOps / Legal confirm whether we can safely offer a short pilot carve-out (US-only, no fallback) and what controls we'd require? I'm attaching the proposed MOU from the customer.

Ask: 1) Product: feasibility and any perf/latency caveats; 2) SecOps/SRE: risk/controls and monitoring; 3) Legal: any contract language or DPA changes we need.

Timeline: CareAtlas wants to start next Monday, 2027-12-13. We should confirm by EOD tomorrow if we can proceed.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment: careatlas_pilot_mou.pdf

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CareAtlas ask — enforce regional variant + no-fallback for initial pilot

Thanks Marcus — I pulled Product in to evaluate the SLO/rollback impact. A few quick notes from my side: 

- We can technically pin routing at the gateway so that CareAtlas traffic is forced to the specified variant and region. That part is straightforward.
- The real risk is operational: no-fallback means if the variant pool becomes degraded or overloaded, requests will fail rather than silently degrade to a compatible variant. We need explicit retry/queueing limits and a fast rollback path that flips routing to a safe fallback if outages spike beyond a threshold.
- For a short pilot we can accept that risk if Control/Monitoring is in place and the customer signs a risk acknowledgment.

Grace — can you share the minimum telemetry and alerting we need to commit to (latency/5xx thresholds, queue depth triggers, KV cache warm-up checks)? Also attaching a first-pass checklist I pulled together.

Evelyn
Director, Platform Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: variant-security-checklist.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 13:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CareAtlas ask — enforce regional variant + no-fallback for initial pilot

Team —

From a security/compliance standpoint we need to be explicit about three things before we greenlight a no-fallback carve-out:

1) Data residency enforcement: confirm that logs, KV cache and any temporary state remain within the US regional tenancy for this customer — and document the enforcement mechanism.
2) Audit trail: every forced-route decision must be logged with request id, route selected, and any attempted fallback (even if disabled) so we can reconstruct incidents.
3) Risk acceptance: Legal must capture that the customer accepts increased outage risk as part of the MOU. We'll also require a short window (48 hours) for us to rehearse the rollback in staging with a simulated load prior to production cutover.

If Product is ok with telemetry hooks, SecOps can stand up the extra alerts (we'll need a temporary escalation runbook). I don't want this to become an open-ended platform change — limit the carve-out to the pilot window and include an automatic expiry.

Rishi
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CareAtlas ask — enforce regional variant + no-fallback for initial pilot

Marcus / Evelyn —

Legal is OK in principle with a limited technical carve-out for a time-boxed pilot, provided we get: 1) signed MOU with explicit risk acknowledgment language; 2) a scope that ties the carve-out to the account ID and project tag so it cannot be re-used; and 3) a clause that allows automatic rollback by Redwood if platform health indicators cross agreed thresholds (we'll propose precise thresholds).

Please have Sales add the following language to the MOU draft under "Pilot Constraints":
- "Customer acknowledges that Redwood may enforce a single model variant for the Pilot and disable automatic fallback. Customer accepts the risk of increased request failures resulting from the variant binding. Redwood reserves the right to revert routing to a safe fallback variant without prior notice if platform health indicators exceed agreed thresholds."

Once Marcus gets a signed MOU back from Samira, Legal will prepare a short amendment to the standard DPA (if needed) and confirm whether exec approval is required for SLA exceptions.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@careatlas.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CareAtlas ask — enforce regional variant + no-fallback for initial pilot

Team / Samira —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Recap of what we agreed internally and the path forward (please flag if I missed anything):

- Scope: 6-week US-only pilot for CareAtlas, traffic pinned to quantized-v2-us-compact. No automatic fallback during pilot, except an automated emergency rollback triggered by platform-health thresholds (as Legal suggested).
- Controls: SecOps to enable region-only residency and the audit trail for forced-routing decisions. Grace to publish the telemetry thresholds (latency, 5xx rate, queue depth) and to lead a 48-hour staging rollback rehearsal next week.
- Legal: Customer will sign an MOU with the exact pilot language Lauren proposed. Legal will prepare any short DPA amendment if needed.
- Timeline: Staging rehearsal Wednesday 2027-12-15; production cutover earliest 2027-12-20 after rehearsal and signed MOU.

Samira — can you confirm that CareAtlas will sign the MOU by Tuesday EOD? If so we'll lock resources for the staging drill.

Thanks again — I will open an ops-runbook ticket and share the link once created.

Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick reply. Yes, we need a single-variant guarantee for our QA runs. We'll sign the MOU and include the risk acknowledgment. Can you also add an explicit clause that the variant binding will not be changed during the run window except for emergency rollback by Redwood?

Samira Khan
VP of Product, CareAtlas Health
